osaka_panaf_african_restaurant_club.notes: [African · Amerikamura, the Expo's African restaurant, now a buffet with live music] The African restaurant that drew crowds at the 2025 Osaka Expo, reopened on the 7th floor of Big Step in Amerikamura and since October 2026 a buffet: ¥2,000 at lunch, ¥3,800 at dinner, with a terrace and live African music every night. Try the peanut-rich mafe stew, Kenyan kebab, kataifi shrimp and the rice dishes, and a baobab or bissap juice. Diners in 2026 found it great value and fun; some found the entry queue disorganised, the soups sour or the popular dishes gone at peak times. On Friday and Saturday nights it turns into a club until 5:00.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: an African buffet restaurant with live performances, blending traditional African culture with contemporary flavours, with dishes that were a hit at the Expo; buffet from 2 October 2026; opened 24 March 2026. October 2026 reviewers describe it as the African restaurant from the Osaka Kansai Expo.
chef_bio.philosophy: Refined African dishes that break the stereotype of Africa (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I especially loved the Mafe, a rich beef stew made with peanut butter, which had a wonderful buttery aroma." — October 2026, buffet with craft beer ¥6,500.
"The performers shared stories about their country's culture." — October 2026, the ¥2,500 lunch with drinks.
"There was a long line at the reception. It felt more like the operation was not well organized rather than a shortage of staff." — October 2026, Saturday lunch.

osaka_yamatoya_honten_shimanouchi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Sashimi is the plainest; fugu kara-age, sukiyaki and the sauces are wheat or soy based. The shop takes requests for children's meals (Tabelog).

Reservations; groups of 15–16 or more by phone; rooms for two hours (Tabelog). Kaiseki courses: Umai kaiseki ¥6,600, Ookini course ¥7,700, Tenkomori with fugu, Kobe beef and Ise lobster ¥13,200 (Tabelog). BYO drinks allowed; children's lunch sets and meals on request (Tabelog). osaka_yamatoya_honten_shimanouchi.notes: [Kaiseki · Shimanouchi, seasonal Kansai kaiseki by the Dotonbori River] A large Japanese restaurant (and inn) on the Dotonbori River just across Nipponbashi, with fully private rooms for anything from two to a hundred guests, popular for company trips and New Year parties. Courses follow the season: kue hot pot in winter, hamo in summer, Kobe beef, fugu, and a ¥13,200 boat-platter feast of fugu, Kobe beef and Ise lobster. Diners praise the sashimi and the private rooms; several found the service rushed or ordinary for the setting, and one found the abalone disappointing (July 2026). Menus in four languages; lunch and dinner daily.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: by the Dotonbori River, serving seasonal dishes from carefully selected ingredients so guests can taste Kansai's "shun"; rooms for groups of 2 to 100. An April 2026 reviewer describes staying at Yamatoya as a ryokan with a public bath; June 2026 reviewers came on a company trip.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal kaiseki; fugu and kue hot pots.

anecdotes.text: "I was particularly impressed by the Kue hot pot, which had a superb broth and wonderfully tender texture." — December 2024, the kue kaiseki at lunch.
"The MVP was the flounder wrapped in paper." — June 2026, a company trip.
"We also had abalone, but it tasted more like tokobushi." — July 2026, a company-trip dinner.

osaka_osteria_pantera_shinsaibashi.notes: [Italian · Shinsaibashi, an all-day osteria by Daimaru] A stylish osteria a minute from Daimaru Shinsaibashi, open from morning to late night, with fresh pasta at lunch and small plates and over 50 wines in the evening. Start with the four-cheese and honey focaccia and the fig, prosciutto and burrata plate, then a porcini or tomato-cream fresh pasta and the beef steak with porcini sauce. chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: fresh pasta at lunch and small plates and meat dishes with over 50 wines in the evening; courses for gatherings and dates; a sommelier. An October 2026 diner says it reopened on 26 September 2026 and now opens from 8:00 for breakfast.

osaka_tachizushi_sugio_nishinakajima.notes: [Sushi · Nishinakajima, a standing sushi bar open past 2 a.m.] A bright, lively standing sushi bar in an alley near Nishinakajima-Minamigata, where the chefs make each piece in front of you and you order one at a time, from ¥132 (Tabelog). The rice is small and the toppings big, so you can try many: uni, akami, three kinds of salmon, then ikura and rolls (2026). Start with a beer and the homemade milk tofu or some grilled fish (2026). It is open until 2:30, a favourite last stop before the final train (September–October 2026). Opinions vary on value; some found it pricey for the quality (July 2026). Closed Sunday.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog shop text: a casual standing sushi bar two minutes from Nishinakajima-Minamigata, where skilled chefs make authentic sushi in front of you with attention to freshness, thickness and preparation of the toppings. Reviewers: reliable, lively service (July 2026); a known spot in the area for years (September 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Freshness, thickness and preparation of the toppings (Tabelog shop text).

anecdotes.text: "The rice is on the smaller side, which is a great point because it allows you to enjoy a variety of toppings in small portions!" — October 2026.
"One of the dishes I was looking forward to was the 'homemade milk tofu'." — June 2026.
"It's great that they're open until late, allowing me to stop by for a quick delicious bite before the last train!" — September 2026.

osaka_komeya_cocoya_nishinakajima.notes: [Izakaya · Nishinakajima, an izakaya where the rice is the star] An izakaya near Nishinakajima-Minamigata, open since 2004, run around rice: the owner, a certified rice taster, chooses the grain, and it is cooked in a clay pot to order, glossy and sweet (shop site; 2026). Pair it with 40–50 junmai sakes and dishes made for rice, such as salt-koji kara-age, chicken nanban and the house mapo curry (2026). Lunch is a ¥1,000 kara-age and pork-soup set; dinner courses run about ¥4,500 (2026). Smoking is allowed, so no children.

chef_bio.background: Shop site: COCOYA (※米屋) is an izakaya themed on enjoying rice; the owner is a certified rice and taste appraiser (米・食味鑑定士) and buys rice selected at a five-star rice meister's shop in the city; the rice is cooked in a clay pot made for rice; 40–50 junmai sakes; the mapo curry was featured on Kansai TV programmes in 2019. Opened 3 April 2004 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: The appeal of rice beyond plain white rice (shop site).

anecdotes.text: "Most importantly, the star of the meal, the white rice, is cooked for 30 minutes after ordering, reflecting their dedication." — September 2026, pork kara-age and tonjiru set for JPY 1,000.
"Towards the end, they served glossy white rice cooked in a pot." — October 2026.
"The Mapo Curry was also incredibly tasty, and I couldn't put my chopsticks down." — October 2026, lunch.

osaka_kawakita_shoten_shin_osaka.notes: [Yakitori · Shin-Osaka Station, mince skewers and a long happy hour] A busy yakitori counter in the food hall by the subway exit at Shin-Osaka Station, popular with travellers killing time before the Shinkansen, thanks to a happy hour from 11:00 to 18:00 with drinks from ¥290 (October 2026). Order the signature Kawakita mince skewers, coarse chicken with crunchy cartilage, five for ¥590, with salt or the richer sauce (2026). Lunch is a generous chicken nanban set for about ¥1,100 (2026). One diner found the skewers uneven when the kitchen was busy (September 2026). Open daily to 23:00.

Stairs are narrow and steep (March and October 2026). Opened 1 May 2019 (Tabelog).
osaka_hoshizora_kitchen_nova.notes: [Italian · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, creative Italian until 5 a.m.] A two-storey Italian bar three minutes from Shinsaibashi Station, with a long, high-ceilinged counter downstairs and hideaway sofa rooms above in a space the shop says was designed by Tadao Ando. It runs from 6 p.m. to 5 a.m., so it serves both early dinners and late-night wine with an appetizer platter (the mackerel with white-miso eggplant sauce stands out). Diners praise the Bolognese, carbonara and shrimp bread and the friendly staff; courses suit birthdays and girls' nights but keep a strict two-hour limit. Mind the narrow, steep stairs: one October 2026 diner sprained an ankle. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Shop-maintained Tabelog listing: casual creative Italian and wine; reservation-only courses; a two-storey designer space that the listing says was designed by the architect Tadao Ando, with a long counter on 1F and private sofa seating above; opened 1 May 2019.

anecdotes.text: "Everything was delicious, but the Bolognese was exceptionally good!" — April 2026.
"The mackerel was served with a sauce made from dried tomatoes, eggplant, and white miso." — October 2026, at the bar until 5 a.m.
"Also, be careful of the steps; I tripped and ended up spraining my ankle, which required a visit to the hospital." — October 2026.

osaka_cafe_mode_minamihorie.notes: [Café · Minami-Horie, an all-day café over Horie Park] A bright white café on the third floor of a building facing Horie Park, with big windows onto the trees, and cherry blossoms in spring. It serves lunch sets all day, from a Kobe beef steak assiette and a filler-free hamburg to beef stew, pasta and avocado toast, plus an evening set of pork shabu-shabu or simmered flounder. The cakes are the other reason to come: the pear cake, a light mille-feuille, and a gluten-free caramel pear tart one March 2026 diner enjoyed (ask, as the menu changes). Dogs are welcome inside. Order and pay at the counter. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog: café, Italian and steak on 3F of the 中澤唐木ビル by Horie Park; lunch sets all day; private hire up to 120; ingredients and suppliers may change with weather and logistics. Reviews (March–September 2026): an Italian café in a bright, bridal-feeling space by the park.

"Dogs are welcome inside the restaurant." — September 2026.

osaka_yakiniku_house_tarareba_nishinakaj.notes: [Yakiniku · Minamikata, whole-cow Kagoshima wagyu over charcoal] A 35-seat yakiniku house two minutes from Hankyu Minamikata, opened in 2024, that buys whole Kagoshima black wagyu, A5 female cattle, and grills it over charcoal. That means rare cuts like misuji and kainomi alongside thick tongue and a big sukiyaki-style ribeye with egg yolk; brave diners also order tongue or harami sashimi (2026). Solo diners get half portions at the ground-floor counter; groups sit upstairs on sunken kotatsu, with courses from ¥4,500. Order by tablet. Open to 23:00; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: yakiniku and offal; opened 2 September 2024. Per reviews: "specializes in Kagoshima A5 rank black-haired Wagyu beef with a BMS score of 10 or higher" (September 2026); whole-cattle buying gives "rare parts that are hard to find elsewhere" (August 2026); "the staff provides excellent service, always smiling and accommodating even when dealing with tipsy patrons" (September 2026); a regular on the fifteenth visit (September 2026); one diner booked the counter and was seated upstairs (October 2026); upstairs table chairs bump together (September 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Whole-cow Kagoshima A5 wagyu; tongue three ways.

osaka_shiki_shizen_tachibana_shin_osaka.notes: [Izakaya · Shin-Osaka, a big Japanese banquet house with homemade tofu] A 200-seat Japanese restaurant on the second floor of the Nissei building, reached under cover from Shin-Osaka exit 4, with private rooms and a tatami hall for 120. Its pride is homemade tofu: at lunch, sets of sashimi or dashimaki and tempura come with zaru or chilled tofu and free refills of tofu, rice and soup, around ¥1,450–1,600 (2025–2026). Evenings turn to banquet courses with all-you-can-drink from ¥5,000, sashimi and seasonal Osaka water eggplant. Busy with office workers at noon. Open to 23:00 on weekdays.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: izakaya, seafood and fugu; particular about fish; health menu; private rooms; reached directly from Shin-Osaka exit 4 "without worrying about rain". A second shop in Umeda (Hilton Plaza, per Hot Pepper; "I had been to Tachibana in Umeda for dinner before", July 2026). Per reviews: "The signature dish, homemade tofu, boasts a smooth texture and rich soybean flavor" (June 2026); "even after the all-you-can-drink time was over, I could extend it for an hour by ordering a la carte" (June 2026); the tatami room suited a family with a baby (August 2026); one diner found the overseas staff short on smiles (July 2026).

anecdotes.text: "I imagined the cold zaru tofu, so I was surprised when it was warm! But eating it with the dashi was refreshing." — June 2026, simmered fish set.
"Chilled tofu, rice, and soup are all refillable." — September 2026.
"The seasonal water eggplant from Osaka was delicious." — June 2026.

osaka_teppanyaki_mydo_w_osaka.notes: [Teppanyaki · Shinsaibashi, W Osaka's playful Osaka teppan] W Osaka's ground-floor teppanyaki, named after the Osaka greeting "maido", where wagyu, lobster and abalone come alongside teppan versions of Osaka street food like okonomiyaki, kushikatsu and akashiyaki. The weekday lunch course at ¥5,500 is the easy way in; dinner courses run to ¥30,000–50,000+ plus 15% service. Smart casual; children under 12 at lunch only. One August 2026 diner found the top course lacked impact for the price.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing and ikyu: the teppanyaki restaurant on the 1st floor of W Osaka, with LUXE, FUN and KAPPO areas; the name reportedly comes from the Osaka greeting "maido" (May 2026 review); interior by designer Yasumichi Morita and art by Seitaro Kuroda (search result).
chef_bio.specialty: Teppan wagyu with Osaka soul food.

anecdotes.text: "Is this really it!? You can enjoy so much for just JPY 5500! This weekday-only lunch course includes domestic lean meat, okonomiyaki, and spaghetti napolitan." — September 2026.

osaka_cafe_bohemia_shinsaibashi.notes: [Cafe · Nishi-Shinsaibashi, Turkish-lamp cafe from breakfast to midnight] A spacious, dim cafe under hundreds of Turkish lamps on the ground floor of a Sheraton hotel near Shinsaibashi, open from breakfast until midnight. Come for the shrimp coconut curry, hummus or tandoori chicken, or late for a parfait and mint tea; some evenings bring belly-dance shows on the back stage. Reviewers find it calm and good value in the day, though some find the food salty, and the smell of shisha smoked by other guests made one pair leave (October 2025).

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a cafe with Middle Eastern (Turkish), Italian and cafe dishes, breakfast, a stage and live music, opened 5 January 2018 in what is now the Four Points Flex by Sheraton Osaka Shinsaibashi. A July 2026 hotel guest ate breakfast there. An October 2026 diner heard of a Turkish-lamp workshop.

anecdotes.text: "Escape the hustle and bustle of Shinsaibashi at the exotic Cafe BOHEMIA, adorned with stunning Turkish lamps." — May 2026, a ¥750 parfait.
"There’s a stage in the back where they sometimes have belly dancing performances." — September 2026, gin drinks and chorizo.

osaka_benkei_hotel_nikko_osaka.gf_detail: Ask. Tabelog says allergy information is available. The cooking centres on dashi and the sets include tempura and fried dishes; sashimi and sushi are the plainest, with soy sauce to ask about.
osaka_benkei_hotel_nikko_osaka.vegan_detail: Ask in advance. Tabelog lists vegan options, but the regular kaiseki is built on dashi and fish.

A Japanese breakfast is also served, with rolled omelette cooked to order (July 2026). Service charge 15% (Tabelog). Reservations; cancel by the day before; the sushi counter is for children of primary-school age and up (Tabelog). Lunch sets (tax included, before service): weekday "body support" lunch ¥3,950, five-kind sashimi gozen ¥5,800, seasonal three-tier bento ¥6,800 (Tabelog); sushi course Daihoji ¥16,000 (December 2025). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), IC cards, WAON and QR (Tabelog). 78 seats with a counter of a 250-year-old single slab; private rooms for 8, 10 and up to 32 (room fee for groups of 5 or fewer: ¥5,500 at lunch, ¥11,000 at dinner); non-smoking; hotel parking (Tabelog). English menu; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog).
osaka_benkei_hotel_nikko_osaka.notes: [Kaiseki · Shinsaibashi, Hotel Nikko Osaka's Japanese restaurant] The Japanese restaurant on the third floor of Hotel Nikko Osaka, reached straight from Shinsaibashi Station, with windows over the Midosuji ginkgo trees, a sushi counter cut from a 250-year-old slab, and private rooms. Lunch is the easy way in: the seasonal three-tier bento at ¥6,800 or the five-sashimi gozen; dinner brings seasonal kaiseki and a ¥16,000 sushi course. Diners praise the dashi, the sashimi and the attentive staff; one found plates cleared while still being eaten (November 2025). 15% service charge.

chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: seasonal kaiseki centred on the traditional dashi handed down by Chef Yoshida Masao for 35 years, served on the third floor of Hotel Nikko Osaka; Tabelog gives the opening day as 7 July 2015. The listing does not say whether the chef still leads the kitchen.
chef_bio.philosophy: Authentic Japanese cuisine focused on ingredients and dashi (Tabelog).

Order by the piece from the seasonal boards, eel, conger, red snapper, uni, or take a set; the ¥1,210 nigiri lunch of eight pieces and a roll with clam soup is good value for the station (October 2026). Side dishes such as braised sea bream and chawanmushi are worth adding (2026). Some find it no better than a good conveyor-belt shop, and sushi can be slow when busy (2026). Takeout available.

osaka_ram_generation_nishinakajima.notes: [Lamb · Nishinakajima, fresh grass-fed lamb on a thick iron plate] A retro hideaway near Nishinakajima-Minamigata that grills fresh Australian grass-fed lamb, mild with no gamey smell, on thick iron plates (operator site; 2026). Work through thick-cut tongue, chuck eye roll, top sirloin and boneless lamb chops, grill the vegetables in the fat, and finish with yakisoba and a mini lamb curry (2026). The ¥5,500 standard course with all-you-can-drink is the popular choice; lunch sets are cheaper (2026). Book ahead; it can be hot inside in summer.

chef_bio.background: Operator site (羊屋総本舗): all lamb is Australian grass-fed, including Roaring Forties lamb; custom thick iron plates; staff train twice a year on lamb and grill the lamb chops and lamb burgers for guests; a sister restaurant, ラム・ストーリーは突然に, is in Fukushima. Opened 24 November 2020 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Let guests know the true flavour of lamb (operator site).

anecdotes.text: "When you think of lamb, you might imagine a strong gamey taste, but the lamb here is incredibly easy to eat." — September 2026.
"While the dipping sauce was tasty, I also loved the combination of salt and wasabi." — October 2026, standard course for JPY 5,500.
"Additionally, frying vegetables in lamb fat is a great idea." — September 2026.

osaka_bellota_mas_shin_osaka.notes: [Spanish · Shin-Osaka Station, overflowing cava and jamón by the subway gate] A busy little Spanish bar upstairs in Shin-Osaka's 新なにわ大食堂, steps from the Midosuji gate, built for a quick drink: tapas from ¥90, jamón and wine from ¥390 (Tabelog). Start with the "Kobore" cava, poured until it spills over, then the house GYOKURO jamón ibérico and the rotisserie chicken, crisp-skinned and juicy, the dish regulars always order (2026). Happy-hour highballs are ¥190 (October 2026). No bookings; open 10:00 to 23:00 every day.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog shop text: a cheap, fast, delicious standing Spanish bar inside Shin-Osaka Station, "Bellota style" being jamón and Spanish wine with the famous roast chicken; drop in and leave quickly, as in Spain. Opened 30 March 2016 (Tabelog). An October 2026 diner says the company brands its own GYOKURO jamón; a Kyoto bar named ベジョータ ムチョ appears in search results (2026-11-02).

anecdotes.text: "The performance of pouring the sparkling wine to the brim of the glass, and even overflowing into the square coaster below, was truly impressive." — October 2026, Kobore cava.
"The rotisserie chicken features a crispy, fragrant skin and juicy meat, with the delicious juices soaking into the potatoes." — August 2026.
"During happy hour, highballs are just JPY 190." — October 2026.

osaka_yanaken_boo_shin_osaka.notes: [Izakaya · Shin-Osaka Station, salt-seared katsuo by the Shinkansen gate] A stylish Japanese bar run by a liquor shop, right beside the Shinkansen central gate, so close you can drink until a few minutes before your train (2026). The thing to order is the salt-seared katsuo tataki, thick-cut, with coarse salt and wasabi, clean and full of umami (2026). Pair it with a three-sake tasting set or wine; lunch sets combine katsuo, roast beef and chicken nanban for ¥2,500 (September 2026). Two-hour limit; happy hour in the afternoon. Open daily 11:00–22:00; takeout bento too.

chef_bio.background: No shop description on Tabelog beyond the name: a Japanese bar run directly by a liquor shop. Reviewers: friendly, quick service (August–September 2026); the shop used to be on the ground floor before moving (August 2026).

anecdotes.text: "The thickly sliced fish topped with coarse salt and wasabi had no strange aftertaste or odor, just pure umami." — September 2026, salt katsuo tataki.
"Located inside Shin-Osaka Station, 'yanaken boo' is just a 30-second walk from the Shinkansen ticket gates (laughs)." — September 2026.
"I ordered the Yanaken Boo Set Meal for JPY 2500, which included a generous serving of bonito tataki, roast beef, and chicken nanban." — September 2026, lunch.

osaka_tebasaki_no_hane_namba.notes: [Izakaya · Nambanaka, chicken wings and motsunabe by Nankai Namba] A chicken izakaya a minute from Nankai Namba Station, open since 2010 and until midnight every day. Smoking is allowed, so children cannot enter. No cards; PayPay only. Sister shop in Shinsekai.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog, opened 1 September 2010; a Tabelog corporate member shop with a 新世界店 under the same name.
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken wings; Tajima chicken sashimi; beef motsunabe.

anecdotes.text: "The tebasaki is highly recommended, and indeed it was crispy and juicy—definitely worth trying." — March 2024.
"Despite the restaurant's name suggesting wings, the tebasaki (chicken wings) were on the lean side." — December 2024.
"The young staff were attentive and provided excellent service, which I appreciated." — October 2026.

osaka_noeud_the_chefs_minamisenba.notes: [French · Minami-Senba, Noeud.TOKYO's Osaka sister] A French restaurant on the ground floor of KOKOHOTEL Osaka Shinsaibashi, opened in January 2023 as the Osaka sister of Noeud.TOKYO; 'nœud' means 'connection'. The kitchen uses vegetables from contracted Kansai farms down to leaves, stems and peel, composts the rest, and serves game culled as pests. Diners in 2026 praise the salmon tartare, the all-carrot plate and homemade bread with sesame and apple butter, and found the calm room mostly Japanese; one found some plates hard to eat. Every course has a vegan dish, and a full vegan course is offered.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog, opened 18 January 2023 in Osaka as a sister restaurant to Noeud.TOKYO; the chef chooses seasonal produce from contracted farmers, mainly in western Japan, and uses parts usually thrown away. A November 2025 diner says Noeud.tokyo has been Michelin-listed four years running.
chef_bio.philosophy: The restaurant on Tabelog: make full use of the harvest so the growers' intentions are honoured; fish are bought without fixing the species to protect stocks.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal French courses from Kansai produce; vegan course.

anecdotes.text: "From the leaves and stems of the turnip to the skins of the apples, everything is treated with care" — January 2026.
"There were a few moments where the presentation made them slightly difficult to eat." — December 2025.
"I enjoyed a Halloween Afternoon Tea." — October 2026.

osaka_spice_king_8848_hakuromachi.notes: [Izakaya · Hakuromachi, spice izakaya in a Shinsaibashi alley] A spice izakaya opened in May 2024, hidden at the back of a narrow alley just east of the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade; a sign on the arcade points the way. A May 2026 diner says all the staff are from abroad and it seems family-run; an October 2026 diner found the 'normal' curry quite sweet.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog, opened 15 May 2024; an izakaya menu seasoned with spices, small curries to go with drinks, and wines chosen to suit Indian food.

osaka_pasta_plus_en_to_en_itachibori.vegan_detail: A plant-based omakase of three seasonal appetizers is offered, Tabelog lists vegan options, and lunch pastas have included a seasonal vegetable pasta (Tabelog menu; May 2026 review). Ask about egg in the fresh pasta.
osaka_pasta_plus_en_to_en_itachibori.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 9:00–21:00 (last order 20:30); Sun 9:00–15:30 (last order 15:00); closed Monday and the day after a holiday; breakfast sets 9:00–11:00 (Tabelog). Same-day, seat-only and 5+ bookings by phone; online booking for courses only (official site). Cards, iD, PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY. Non-smoking. English menu and English-speaking staff; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog).
osaka_pasta_plus_en_to_en_itachibori.notes: [Italian · Itachibori, homemade fresh pasta all day] A pasta workshop and Italian dining room on Naniwa-suji, opened in April 2022 and open from 9 AM; the name is read 'Pasta Più' (パスタピュ). Pasta, bread and cakes are made in house; the shop imports its own olive oil, sells frozen pasta, and offers a plant-based appetizer plate. Diners in 2026 praise the fresh tagliatelle, ravioli and mushroom cream, attentive service and shared plates; one found the clams and bottarga flat, and the cheese dishes did not suit one family.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site, PASTA+ is a pasta workshop with food and goods for sale, "Più" meaning it is not only pasta; Italian food built on flavours that put Italians at ease, everything including bread and cakes made in house; frozen pasta featured in あまから手帖 (August 2026 issue) and stalls at the Harukas Kintetsu main store in October 2026. Operated by Remix Co., Ltd. (Tabelog); opened 21 April 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Italian food that makes Italians feel at home" (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The name is pronounced 'Pasta Pyu.'" — June 2026.
"The homemade fresh pasta was truly delightful." — May 2026.
"The clams themselves had no flavor, and the bottarga lacked richness." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (pasta-entoen.net): PASTA＋ (パスタピュ Pasta Più)、パスタ工房と飲食物販の店、「＋」はパスタだけではないという意味、イタリア人がほっとする味、パンやケーキも全て店内で手作り、業務用パスタのOEMも。当日・席のみ・5名以上の予約は電話、各サイトはコースのみ。2026年10月8日〜13日にハルカス近鉄本店の催しに出店、あまから手帖8月号で冷凍パスタが紹介。食べログ (英語版): 西区立売堀2-4-4 永瑞ビル 1F、西大橋駅1番出口から徒歩6分、2022年4月21日オープン、火〜土9:00〜21:00、日9:00〜15:00 (L.O.)、月・祝翌日休み、英語メニューと英語のスタッフ、禁煙。メニュー (2026年7月): 季節の前菜3種1,500円 (植物性のおまかせ3種も可)、トルテッリーニ、じゃがいものニョッキ、土佐あかうしのラザニア、朝のホットサンドとエッグベネディクト、ディナーコース6,600〜11,000円。口コミ (2026年): 手打ちのタリアテッレ、ラビオリ、きのこのクリーム、自家輸入のオリーブオイル、丁寧な接客、取り分け、あさりとからすみが物足りないという声、チーズの料理が口に合わなかったという声。

osaka_umasou_na_ramen_ya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; mazesoba too.
osaka_umasou_na_ramen_ya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: broth simmered from chicken, pork and beef; chicken and pork chashu.
osaka_umasou_na_ramen_ya.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:45) and 18:00–21:00 (last order 20:45); temporary closures on Instagram (Tabelog). No reservations; ticket machine, which did not take ¥1,000 notes (October 2026); cash or PayPay, no cards (Tabelog). No charge (Tabelog). Opened May 10, 2023 (Tabelog). 16 seats: 8 at the counter, 8 at tables; non-smoking (Tabelog). Queues of about 4–6 at lunch and weekend evenings (2023–2026). A stamp card gives a free bowl after three visits (October 2026).
osaka_umasou_na_ramen_ya.notes: [Ramen · Umeda, Taiyujicho, creamy chicken paitan in a basement] A sixteen-seat basement ramen shop near Higashi-Umeda, opened in 2023, with a café look and a queue at lunch. The draw is a creamy, frothy paitan simmered from chicken, pork and beef, in shoyu or salt, with low-temperature chicken and pork chashu and sweet onion hidden underneath; finish the small pool of broth over rice with toasted cheese. About ¥1,000–1,200; an autumn Taiwanese mazesoba (not spicy) has its own fans. Most diners rave about the richness; one longtime visitor found less soup and drier chashu in October 2026. Ticket machine; cash or PayPay.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): a hidden ramen shop 7 minutes from Higashi-Umeda, in a basement with a café vibe, for solo diners to enjoy chicken paitan ramen. Opened May 10, 2023. An October 2026 diner read the shop's notes on simmering chicken, pork and beef for eight hours.

anecdotes.text: "One sip and you're overwhelmed by its intense creaminess, surpassing even Tenkaippin." — October 2026.
"The noodles had a low water content, providing the perfect texture and bite." — October 2026.
"The chashu, both chicken breast and pork chuck eye roll, was overcooked and dry compared to before." — October 2026, a return visit.

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket machine; staff take orders in the queue (October 2026). No English evidence found.

osaka_torisho_akatsuki_togano.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Skewers are salted to suit each cut, some with sauces; cartilage kara-age and oyakodon are on the menu.
osaka_torisho_akatsuki_togano.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken, with mizutaki in a chicken broth; grilled seasonal vegetables are on the menu, and Tabelog lists vegetarian options with no detail.
osaka_torisho_akatsuki_togano.hours_raw: Tabelog: Mon–Fri 17:00–2:00 (food last order 1:00); Sat 17:00–24:00; holidays 17:00–23:00; closed Sundays, plus some days at Obon and New Year; open until ingredients run out. The official site gives dinner 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00) and lunch 11:30–14:00 (Tue–Fri on one page); the two differ. Bookings for two may be seated at the counter; 2-hour limit when busy (Tabelog). Appetizer ¥330 (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 22 seats; heated tobacco only inside, an ashtray for cigarettes at the entrance (Tabelog).
osaka_torisho_akatsuki_togano.notes: [Yakitori · Togano-cho, morning-fresh chicken over binchotan] A twenty-two-seat yakitori izakaya in Togano-cho, east of Umeda, built on chicken slaughtered that morning and grilled over Kishu binchotan, with the chef adjusting salt and time for each cut. Start with a chicken sashimi platter and the limited white-liver sashimi, then skewers like negima and egg-yolk tsukune, grilled seasonal vegetables, and a creamy oyakodon or the milky collagen soup to finish; in winter there is a mizutaki hot pot. Courses with drinks are ¥5,000–6,000, good value for the area. Tabelog lists hours to 2 am on weekdays, the shop's site 23:00.

roles: Chef and manager (unnamed) at the grill (2025–2026)
chef_bio.background: Official site: morning-slaughtered chicken grilled over top-grade Kishu binchotan at up to 1,000°C; cut, skewered and grilled differently for each ingredient; seasonal vegetables direct from producers; oyakodon is the regulars' favourite finish; hot pot in winter. Tabelog shop text: the chef personally grills every skewer, adjusting saltiness and time for each part.
chef_bio.philosophy: Yakitori made with care and no shortcuts (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The chef skillfully grills in silence, exuding coolness." — December 2025.
"The limited quantity of white liver stands out, along with the fresh chicken sashimi" — January 2026.
"To finish off, I had the 'Fluffy and Creamy Oyakodon' and 'Milky Collagen Soup'!" — November 2025.

osaka_dojima_kirazu.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Lunch trays include tempura and kakiage, simmered dishes and miso soup.
osaka_dojima_kirazu.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fish, dashi and egg dishes.
osaka_dojima_kirazu.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:00 and 17:30–22:00; Sat 17:30–22:00; closed Sundays; holidays by reservation; hours may change (Tabelog). Courses by reservation only (Tabelog). The owner runs it alone, so lunch may turn people away when full (February 2025; June 2026).
osaka_dojima_kirazu.notes: [Japanese · 堂島, a one-man kitchen with sake by the dish] An eighteen-seat Japanese restaurant in a hidden house-like space in 堂島 3-chome, open since 2005 and run single-handed by a stern-looking owner. Weekday lunch is a ¥1,100 tray, seasonal, tempura or a seafood bowl, with chawanmushi made to order and a little yokan; regulars call it remarkable value, though one found the tempura heavy. Dinner is the reason to book: seasonal dishes at a sunken counter, each paired with a different, often rare sake from a list of over twenty, plus Italian wines. Shoes off; holidays by reservation only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog remarks: over 20 types of sake and shochu at all times and over 30 wines, mainly Italian. Opened September 13, 2005. Diners: the owner runs the place alone (February 2025); "The owner, who has a somewhat stern demeanor, manages everything" alone (June 2026). The Tabelog listing is not shop-maintained.
chef_bio.specialty: Lunch trays; sake pairing at dinner.

"The chawanmushi (steamed egg custard) was prepared fresh after I placed my order." — July 2025.
"Please note that shoes are not allowed inside." — June 2026.

osaka_shushi_mon_nishitenma.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Signatures include anago tempura with green onion and sweet soy, and a mackerel sandwich; ponzu dishes; a tonkatsu lunch.
osaka_shushi_mon_nishitenma.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seafood and wagyu kappo.
osaka_shushi_mon_nishitenma.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); Sat 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–22:00 (last order 21:30); closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). A May 2026 diner says lunch runs under another name, Shokudo Murakami, with its own Tabelog page, so this listing is for dinner. Bookings for 2 or more (Tabelog). Appetizer ¥660 (Tabelog). Opened April 1, 1995 per Tabelog; moved here from Ohatsu Tenjin (April 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), IC cards, Rakuten Edy, PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay (Tabelog). 14 seats at the counter and tables; non-smoking; wheelchair accessible; children welcome; takeout and delivery (Tabelog). Tabelog izakaya WEST 100 in 2025 and 2026.
osaka_shushi_mon_nishitenma.notes: [Izakaya · Nishi-Tenma, a kappo-grade izakaya by Kitashinchi] A fourteen-seat izakaya just across the road from Kitashinchi, moved here from Ohatsu Tenjin and on Tabelog's izakaya WEST 100 in 2025 and 2026, that cooks like a kappo: thick-cut seasonal sashimi, grilled sawara with caviar, wagyu grilled on a magnolia leaf, hamo somen in summer. Two signatures appear in every course, a crisp anago tempura buried under green onion and a mackerel sandwich with pickled turnip. Courses are ¥11,000–15,000; the young chef wears a sommelier pin and pairs wine and sake. Lunch runs separately as a set-meal shop. One diner disliked the ponzu's seasoning; most found it superb.

roles: Head chef (unnamed), with a sommelier pin (August 2026)
A second cook; one diner guessed the two cooks were father and son, unconfirmed (May 2026)
chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): a kappo izakaya that values communication with customers; seasonal Japanese cuisine with fresh seafood; sake from top breweries and wine chosen by a sommelier; a calm white interior with counter and tables. Opened April 1, 1995 per Tabelog; relocated from Ohatsu Tenjin (April 2026 review). Lunch runs as Shokudo Murakami, with a separate Tabelog page (May 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: A dish that evokes Japanese tradition and the four seasons (Tabelog).
